## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. A sharp selloff in AI and chip stocks led the move, and volatility jumped. Investors bought Treasuries as a haven, and stocks rebounded only partly afterward.

## 2. What moved and why
**AI and chip stocks crater after Democrats win Congress**
Why it happened: AI and semiconductor stocks sold off sharply as investors reassessed the data center build-out after Democrats won control of Congress. Nvidia sank 9.3%, erasing its gains for the year. All 11 S&P 500 sectors closed lower.
Why it matters: The S&P 500 and the Dow both had their worst day since April 2025. The VIX had its biggest one-day surge in almost two years. The market is now questioning how long AI infrastructure spending can keep growing.

**Treasury yields dip on haven demand as Fed hike bets linger**
Why it happened: Treasuries drew haven demand during the selloff. Nerves about AI stocks and bets on a slower data center buildout also supported government bonds.
Why it matters: Rate markets are still debating tightening. Traders had priced in a quarter-point Fed hike for December. Short-dated yields rose after the strong US payrolls report.

**Loonie slides as Canada's job losses extend**
Why it happened: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October, against expectations for a gain of 13,600. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7%. Global equity volatility also weighed on the currency.
Why it matters: Market-implied odds of a Bank of Canada hike in December fell to 35% from 40%. Weak Canadian data alongside strong US data widens the policy gap between the two countries.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Marvell Technology → Lumentum Holdings** (US$115B enterprise value (all-stock)). <cite index="69-2">Marvell is buying Lumentum to capitalize on runaway data center spending.</cite> <cite index="71-2">Marvell shares fell 13% and Lumentum 19% on announcement.</cite> <cite index="69-4">Closing is expected in the first half of 2028.</cite>
- **Acquisition: Blackstone-led investor group (with CPP Investments, OMERS, IMC, PSP) → 49.9% stake in LNG Canada's liquefaction business, from a Mitsubishi unit** ($3.1B as reported). <cite index="43-3,43-4">Blackstone and four Canadian pension investors agreed to buy a Mitsubishi subsidiary's stake in LNG Canada.</cite> It shows infrastructure capital still wants long-life Canadian energy export assets.
- **Acquisition: AMD → Taalas Inc. (Toronto)** (About US$2.9B (cash and stock)). <cite index="46-3">AMD will pay about US$2.9 billion for Toronto-based chip startup Taalas, one of the largest takeovers of a Canadian tech company.</cite> <cite index="46-2">The price was disclosed in a securities filing.</cite>

## 3. What's coming today
Nothing major is scheduled on Saturday and markets are closed. Next week's focus is October US inflation data and how much it shifts expectations for a December Fed hike.

## 4. Canada corner
- <cite index="23-1">The Canadian dollar fell to a nearly three-week low as job losses cooled Bank of Canada hike expectations.</cite>
- <cite index="23-8">The Bank of Canada and finance ministry set a new five-year policy framework and kept the 2% inflation target.</cite>
- <cite index="61-9">Falling crude reversed much of October's price strength for Canadian producers.</cite> <cite index="40-5">Canadian Natural is targeting $800 million a month in share buybacks for November and December.</cite>
- <cite index="44-1">National Bank agreed to buy Embark Student Corp., a digital RESP provider.</cite>

## 5. The takeaway
If someone asks you about markets today: an AI and chip rout, triggered by fears that a Democratic Congress will slow data center building, drove the worst US stock day since April 2025 and sent volatility sharply higher. Canada's weak jobs data weighed on the loonie.
